thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stock Market Falls As Jobs Data Boost Yields

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stock Market Falls As Jobs Data Boost Yields
text:
By Anora M. Gaudiano and Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Dow, S&P 500 face worst weekly performances since late 2016
U.S. stock market indexes were trading lower Friday as investors digested a stronger-than-expected jobs report that saw bond yields continue their climb.
The U.S. economy added 200,000 jobs in January (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-adds-2 -jobs-worker-pay-rises-at-fastest-pace-since-2009-2018-02-02)with the best news coming from the wage growth. Average hourly wages rose 0.3%, pushing the yearly increase to 2.9%, the fastest pace in more than eight years.
Analysts said the market is pricing in tighter monetary policy if inflation driven by wage growth accelerates.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
The S&P 500 index was off by 22 points, or 0.8%, to 2,798 and looked set for a 2.4% weekly decline. Losses on Wall Street were broad-based with 10 of the 11 main sectors trading lower. Energy and technology shares led the declines, down more than 1%, while consumer-discretionary stocks were the only bright spot, up 0.7%.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell below the psychologically important 26,000 level, trading 234points, or 0.9%, lower to 25,946.
The Nasdaq Composite Index slid 60 points, or 0.8%, to 7,328.
A couple of bruising sessions this week, including Friday's declines have left their mark on the main indexes, with the S&P 500 and Dow looking for the worst weekly performance in more than a year.
What are strategists saying?
"A big wage growth number is the biggest risk to the stock market rally, because it means the Fed may get more aggressive in raising interest rates," said Kristina Hooper, chief global market strategist at Invesco.
"The details of this jobs report, especially the numbers behind the wage growth suggest that companies are competing for workers and the shortage of skilled workers is pushing up wages. The trend in inflation is ticking higher and the big question is whether the incoming Fed, which is more hawkish, will allow the economy run hotter in the short term," said Quincy Krosby, chief market strategist, at Prudential Financial.
Other analysts said that higher bond yields will result in the stock market repricing.
The markets are coming to grip with the fact that a 3-3.25% yield factor is not far away. In summary. higher yields will continue to keep pressure on stocks," Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at First Standard Financial, said in a note to clients, referring to the 10-year Treasury rate.
Which stocks look like key movers?
Shares in Amazon Inc.(AMZN) climbed 7% after the e-commerce retailer posted fourth-quarter profit and revenue that blew past forecasts.

(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/deutsche-bank-dragged-to-loss-by-us-tax-hit-2018-02-02) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/deutsche-bank-dragged-to-loss-by-us-tax-hit-2018-02-02)Exxon Mobil Corp.(XOM) earnings fell short of estimates, despite tax benefit. Shares were down 5.1%.
Phillips 66 (PSX) shares fell 1.2% even as the company released earnings above Wall Street's expectations.
J.C. Penney Co.(JCP) shares dropped 1.1% after quarterly earnings release.
What could help drive markets?
Stocks were taking a hit as global government bond yields, which have dogged stocks this week, continued to climb on Friday. The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note rose to a four-year high at 2.83%.
Meanwhile, the yield on 10-year German government bunds added 4 basis points to reach 0.690%, close to levels not seen in more than two years. Higher returns on debt securities tend to weaken appetite for stocks and other assets perceived as risky.
Read: U.S. adds 200,000 jobs with wage growth fastest in more than 8 years (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-adds-2 -jobs-worker-pay-rises-at-fastest-pace-since-2009-2018-02-02)
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/january-jobs-bonanza-hiring-likely-rebounded-in-early-2018-2018-02-01)Consumer sentiment for January is due at 10 a.m. Eastern, along with factory orders for December.
What are other assets doing?
European stocks slumped, driven by a 1.3% slide for the German DAX (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dax-drops-below-13000-after-deutsche-bank-logs-a-hefty-loss-2018-02-02), in part dogged by Deutsche Bank's hefty loss. Asian markets saw a mixed session, with the Nikkei 225 index down 0.9% on disappointing earnings. Gold was flat, while oil futures inched up, and the ICE U.S. Dollar Index rose to 88.85, thought it is still down 3.6% since the start of the year.
